title: Data Brokers & Data Collection Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect your personal data from brokers. Learn how to opt out, limit collection, and harden your privacy against data selling.
intro: Data brokers collect and sell your personal information from hundreds of sources. This comprehensive checklist helps you identify what data is being collected, opt out from major brokers, and implement protective measures to limit future data harvesting.

items.why: Most people don't realize how much personal information is available online through data brokers until they search for themselves.
items.howTo: Search for your name, address, and phone number on major people search sites like WhitePages, Spokeo, and BeenVerified. Document what information appears publicly.

items.why: Understanding where your data comes from helps you make informed decisions about what services to use and what information to share.
items.howTo: Review your social media privacy settings, loyalty card programs, online purchases, and public records. List services that may be sharing or selling your data.

items.task: Check top 20 data broker websites for your information
items.why: Data brokers profit by selling detailed profiles about you to marketers, employers, and anyone willing to pay for your personal information.
items.howTo: Visit major data broker sites including Acxiom, LexisNexis, Epsilon, and Experian. Search for your information and note what's available for purchase.

items.task: Submit opt-out requests to major data brokers
items.why: Opting out removes your information from broker databases and prevents them from selling your data to third parties.
items.howTo: Use each broker's opt-out process. Most require email verification. Keep records of your requests. Focus on Acxiom, LexisNexis, Epsilon, Experian, and ChoicePoint first.

items.task: Remove your listings from people search engines
items.why: People search sites make your personal information easily discoverable by anyone, including stalkers, identity thieves, and unwanted contacts.
items.howTo: Submit removal requests to WhitePages, Spokeo, BeenVerified, PeopleFinder, Intelius, and TruePeopleSearch. Each has different removal procedures that must be followed exactly.

items.task: Register with DMA Choice to reduce marketing lists
items.why: The Direct Marketing Association helps reduce the amount of commercial mail and email you receive from participating companies.
items.howTo: Visit DMAchoice.org and register your name, address, phone number, and email address. This opt-out service covers many marketing databases at once.

items.task: Switch to a privacy-focused browser for sensitive activities
items.why: Standard browsers collect extensive data about your browsing habits, which is then sold to data brokers and advertisers.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser for sensitive searches and transactions. It blocks trackers by default and doesn't store your browsing data, reducing data collection opportunities.

items.task: Configure strict privacy settings in your main browser
items.why: Default browser settings prioritize functionality over privacy, allowing extensive data collection through cookies and tracking scripts.
items.howTo: Enable strict tracking protection, disable third-party cookies, turn off data sharing with browser company, and regularly clear browsing data. Install uBlock Origin extension.

items.task: Restrict social media data sharing and advertising permissions
items.why: Social media platforms are major sources of personal data for brokers, sharing information about your interests, relationships, and behaviors.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Instagram. Disable ad personalization, limit data sharing with third parties, and restrict profile visibility.

items.task: Freeze your credit reports with all three bureaus
items.why: Credit freezes prevent data brokers and others from accessing your credit information, which contains detailed personal and financial data.
items.howTo: Contact Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion to place security freezes on your credit reports. Keep the PIN numbers secure. Freezes are free and reversible.

items.task: Audit and limit retail loyalty program memberships
items.why: Loyalty programs track your purchases and sell this data to brokers, creating detailed profiles of your spending habits and lifestyle.
items.howTo: Cancel unnecessary loyalty cards and memberships. For programs you keep, opt out of data sharing where possible and use alternate contact information.

items.task: Use privacy-focused payment methods for online purchases
items.why: Payment data reveals detailed information about your lifestyle, preferences, and financial situation to merchants and their data broker partners.
items.howTo: Use virtual credit card numbers when available, consider privacy-focused payment services, and avoid linking purchases to loyalty accounts when possible.

items.task: Set up Google Alerts for your personal information
items.why: New data broker sites appear regularly, and removed information sometimes reappears, requiring ongoing monitoring and action.
items.howTo: Create Google Alerts for your full name, address, phone number, and email address. Review results weekly and submit removal requests for new appearances.

items.task: Review and update privacy settings quarterly
items.why: Companies frequently update their privacy policies and settings, often defaulting to less privacy-protective options after updates.
items.howTo: Schedule quarterly reviews of social media, browser, email, and other online account privacy settings. Document changes and adjust settings to maintain privacy protection.

items.task: Monitor for data breaches affecting your accounts
items.why: Data breaches often lead to increased data broker activity as your information becomes available through new channels.
items.howTo: Use HaveIBeenPwned to check if your email addresses appear in known breaches. Sign up for breach notifications and take immediate action when breaches occur.
